title: bug: three crash windows the delivery-receipt replay does not cover
description:
Named by task-bfe2f04e's self-review as residuals and never filed. The Wave 1 integration gate (task-808869c5) files them. They are combined-failure paths that sit between the ledger, the receipt and the attempt, so no single slice could close them.
1. A hard crash between `update-ref` and `record_commit` loses the ledger row. The next pre-flight's replay records the receipt, but task.commits never gets the completion commit. Under deliveryPolicy local-branch, qa_approve then refuses completion-commit for bytes that did land. Possible fix: the replay also re-sends an idempotent minimal record_commit from the journal, which would need the sessionId journaled.
2. A `pull --rebase` retry inside the push rewrites the pushed commit. The receipt keeps the CAS sha while record_commit keeps the rebased sha. If that receipt is then lost, the replay's `merge-base --is-ancestor` test fails, and it drops the journal with "never moved the ref" although the bytes are on the branch.
3. A foreign seat's replay records the receipt and deletes the journal, but it never finalizes the owner's attempt. That attempt then waits for the owner's deregister or the other close paths.
Code: scripts/moe-agent.ps1 Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay / Send-MoeReceipt, and scripts/moe-agent.sh receipt_replay / receipt_send. See mem:gotcha-wrapper-receipt-journal-and-replay.
definitionOfDone: Each of the three windows is either closed in BOTH wrappers or explicitly accepted with its operator recovery documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md -> Delivery receipts
Every closed window has a postflight arm in both twins that fails on today's wrappers (a crash injected at the named point), and the existing 7 receipt arms stay green
Acceptance criterion 6 stays green unedited; postflight.{sh,ps1} and parity-check.{sh,ps1} pass

PS1 LANDING SIDE (window 1): the journal carries the ledger row that is still owed until record_commit acknowledges it. All changes are in Invoke-MoeLanding.

1. The gated-completion journal is the [ordered] $receipt built just before update-ref, where Write-MoeReceiptJournal is first called. Add ledger=[ordered]@{sessionId=$Sid; role=$Role; status=$Status}.
2. Keep the answer of the committed ledger call (today it is 'Send-MoeRecordCommit $recArgs | Out-Null'):
   $rc = Send-MoeRecordCommit $recArgs; $ledgerAcked = ($null -ne $rc -and (Get-MoeProp $rc 'success') -eq $true)
   Keep '$recorded=$true' unchanged, because the finally block depends on it.
3. In the post-record rewrite ('if ($receipt) { $receipt.pushResult = ...; Write-MoeReceiptJournal ...; Send-MoeReceipt ... }'), remove 'ledger' from $receipt ONLY when $ledgerAcked. Two consequences:
   - A journal left behind by a refused or lost receipt is exactly today's 10-field report. The receipt-refused arm deep-equals it and must stay green unedited.
   - A journal that still carries 'ledger' always means the ledger row may be missing.
4. In Write-MoeReceiptJournal, add -Depth 5 to ConvertTo-Json, because 'ledger' is nested.
5. Leave the finally block's interrupted-landing re-send alone. It keeps the journal as written, so the next replay sends the ledger row once more, and record_commit merges a repeated sha.
6. Do not change Send-MoeReceipt: its payload already takes only the six receipt fields.
7. Update the journal comment above Get-MoeReceiptJournalPath: the journal also carries the owed ledger row until moe.record_commit acknowledges it.

Error handling: a record_commit that returns $null or success != $true leaves 'ledger' in the journal. A journal write that fails keeps today's WARN and never blocks the landing.

PS1 REPLAY (all three windows). Rework Invoke-MoeReceiptReplay. It still runs right after the pre-flight claim, and its per-journal try/catch stays best-effort.

1. VALIDATION: also accept an optional 'ledger'. When present, sessionId must be a non-blank string of at most 255 chars, role a non-blank string of at most 64 chars, and status absent, null or a string. Anything else gets the existing 'kept: malformed journal' WARN.
2. LANDED TEST, in this order:
   a. tip as today: rc 1 means not landed; any other nonzero rc throws and keeps the journal.
   b. 'merge-base --is-ancestor targetAfter tip': rc 0 means landed, with $landedAs = targetAfter; rc > 1 throws.
   c. rc 1 starts the rewritten-copy search:
      - Run 'git log -1 --format=%B <targetAfter>'. A nonzero rc throws 'git log exited N' and keeps the journal.
      - sid is the value of the first 'Moe-Session: ' line, with CR trimmed.
      - If there is a sid, run: git log -n1 --format=%H --fixed-strings --all-match "--grep=Moe-Session: <sid>" '--grep=Moe-Kind: completion' <range>. The range is <targetBefore>..<tip>, or just <tip> when targetBefore is the 40-zero id. A nonzero rc throws.
      - A hit means landed, with $landedAs = hit. Log: [receipt] a pull --rebase rewrote <targetAfter>; <target> carries it as <hit>.
      - No hit keeps today's drop line: 'that landing never moved the ref; dropping'.
   WHY this range is safe: it holds only commits reachable from the tip but not from the CAS base, of kind completion, from this landing's session. A session lands at most one completion. Its pre-flight recovery checkpoint has the same sid but is a wip commit that already sits under the base.
3. OWED LEDGER ROW. After the existing 'replaying the delivery receipt' line, when the journal carries 'ledger':
   a. Send record_commit through Send-MoeRecordCommit with: taskId; outcome 'committed'; kind 'completion'; sha $landedAs; ref = target; role; sessionId; workerId $WorkerId; status (only when non-empty); pushed.
   b. pushed is $false when pushResult is null or starts with 'push failed: ', and $true when it starts with 'pushed '. Omit it for the 'push result unknown' placeholder.
   c. Log: [receipt] recording the owed ledger row of task <tid>: <landedAs> on <target>
   d. Not acknowledged ($null, or success is not $true): WARN 'receipt journal <f> kept: moe.record_commit did not record the owed ledger row', then continue. No receipt and no finalize, so the next pre-flight retries the whole journal.
   e. Acknowledged: remove 'ledger' from $j and rewrite the file with Write-MoeReceiptJournal before the receipt. Otherwise a receipt that keeps being refused would re-send the row on every pre-flight.
4. RECEIPT: unchanged, verbatim through Send-MoeReceipt.
5. FINALIZE FOR ANY SEAT (window 3).
   a. Drop the '$j.workerId -cne $WorkerId' guard.
   b. Give Get-MoePinnedAttemptPhase a 4th parameter [string]$Worker = $WorkerId and use it in its workerId match. Call it with ($j.attemptId, $j.taskId, $j.generation, $j.workerId).
   c. When the phase is 'finalizing', send finalize_attempt with: taskId; attemptId; generation; workerId [string]$j.workerId (the tool contract defines workerId as the seat that held the attempt); runnerId $script:MoeRunnerId; outcome 'landed'; landedRevision $landedAs. Use 3 tries, as today.
   d. The daemon has no owner gate, and the attempt id plus generation fence it.
   e. The failure WARN becomes seat-neutral: 'attempt <aid> is still finalizing after its replayed receipt; its finalizing holds stay until it closes.' It replaces the 'this seat's next claim stays refused' wording.
6. Rewrite the function's header comment to match: any seat closes the attempt, the owed ledger row, the rewritten copy.

Error handling. For every failure, keep the journal and move on to the next journal:
- a git exit code other than the documented 0/1;
- a missing targetAfter object;
- an unacknowledged ledger row;
- a refused receipt.
Only two cases drop a journal: a clean 'not on the target', and no rewritten copy found. The replay never moves a ref, never re-freezes and never re-gates. It never throws out of the pre-flight: the outer catch logs and continues.

docs/CONFIGURATION.md, section 'Delivery receipts', second paragraph:
1. The journal also carries 'ledger' (sessionId, role, status), the ledger row still owed, until moe.record_commit acknowledges it.
2. The replay counts the landing as landed when git shows the journaled revision on the target. It also counts it when git shows its rewritten copy: a commit after the CAS base that carries the landing's Moe-Session and 'Moe-Kind: completion' trailers. A pull --rebase in the push creates that copy.
3. When landed, the replay does three things in order:
   a. It re-sends the owed ledger row. The sha is the commit on the target, there is no path list, and pushed comes from the journaled push result (omitted while unknown).
   b. It re-sends the receipt verbatim.
   c. Whichever seat replays, it closes the journaled attempt as 'landed' while that attempt is still finalizing under the journal's worker.
4. Replace 'for its own journal only'.
5. Add the residuals and their operator recovery in one or two sentences:

     scripts/moe-call.sh record_commit '{"taskId":"<id>","outcome":"committed","kind":"completion","role":"worker","sessionId":"<sid>","sha":"<sha>","ref":"refs/heads/<branch>","pushed":true}' --project <path>
   - An ungated completion writes no journal. A crash after the receipt is recorded but before finalize_attempt also leaves none. In both cases the attempt waits for its worker's deregister_worker, or for the finalize_attempt escape in docs/MCP_SERVER.md.

docs/MCP_SERVER.md, section moe.finalize_attempt: in item 1 of 'Every end of a finalizing attempt', and in the 'Escape for a runner that is gone' note, add this. After a crash, any seat's wrapper that replays the landing's receipt journal closes the attempt as 'landed', and only once git shows the landed revision, or its rewritten copy, on the target.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Put the two wrapper diffs side by side, answer each point below, and post the answers as a task comment.
1. Two seats replay the same journal at once. The ledger re-send merges by sha, the receipt comes back as a duplicate or as DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT, and finalize is idempotent. Confirm nothing lands twice and no ref moves.
2. A live owner is mid-landing. The live-marker skip still runs before any git call or RPC, so a foreign seat never finalizes an attempt whose owner's marker is live, or sits on a host or pid namespace this seat cannot probe.
3. The rewritten-copy search cannot pick up the session's recovery checkpoint (a wip commit, under the base), a peer's commit (another sid), or a landing that never moved the ref (no completion with that sid after the base). Name the guard that covers each.
4. With an unborn target, the range is the tip alone.
5. An old journal without 'ledger' replays exactly as before. A new journal read by an old wrapper loses only the ledger re-send; name this as a mixed-rollout residual.
6. Nothing new runs before claim_next_task, so the single-shot taskless-wait trap (mem:gotcha-single-shot-taskless-wait-vs-crash-replay) is not reopened.
7. The early returns for autoCommit=false, no-git and governor seats are unchanged.
8. No finalize is sent for an attempt whose id, task, generation or worker differs from the journal's.
9. Error handling: every new git call and RPC keeps the journal on failure and never throws out of the pre-flight.
10. moe-agent.sh and postflight.sh are still LF (Serena edits can flip files to CRLF).
11. The existing receipt-replay block and every other pre-existing assertion are byte-identical (check git diff).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
The user confirmed 'close all three' in the REPL.

Window 1, alternatives rejected:
- Read .moe/tasks/<id>.json commits to decide whether the row is owed. This couples the wrapper to the task file format, and the harness fake never persists commits.
- Always re-send record_commit on replay. This breaks receipt-replay's 'exactly one committed row' assertion and posts a duplicate chat line on every pre-flight.
- Journal a bare flag and infer role and status. Journaling the owed row itself keeps the replay verbatim, the same way the receipt is.

Window 2, alternatives rejected:
- Journal a rebasedTo sha after the push. This misses a crash between the rebase and the rewrite, and it would be a second mechanism.
- Rewrite the receipt to the rebased sha. The receipt describes the CAS, and re-sending anything else is exactly what DELIVERY_RECEIPT_CONFLICT refuses.
- Match by patch-id or message equality. This is heavier and gains nothing over the Moe-Session and Moe-Kind trailers the landing already writes and already searches by.

Window 3, alternatives rejected:
- Accept it and rely on a governor's finalize_attempt. A crashed owner usually comes back under a new worker id, so the own-seat replay almost never fires.
- Close it daemon-side. That breaks the state-only rail: the daemon cannot see git.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Daemon contracts:
- finalize_attempt has no ownership gate. It is fenced by attemptId + generation and is idempotent on an already-closed attempt. Its workerId is documented as the seat that held the attempt.
- record_commit merges a repeated sha, upgrading only pushed and treeId. It replaces unattributedPaths only when that field is sent, so the replayed row omits it.
- deliveryPolicy local-branch counts completion rows recorded since the round started. remote-push also needs pushed:true.
- Receipts are display-only (deliveryProjection); no policy reads them.

Landing order in both wrappers: J0 journal, update-ref CAS, push (may pull --rebase), Moe-Session trailer lookup for the sha, record_commit, J1 rewrite, receipt, finalize. Completion landing is worker-only in both twins.

Existing arms pin the current behaviour:
- receipt-refused deep-equals the 10-field J1.
- receipt-replay pins exactly one committed completion row.
- teardown-landed checks three J0 fields.
- The fake finalizeReply refuses a 'landed' finalize unless a matching committed completion row was logged, which is a useful oracle for the new arms.

Harness facts: the frozen-suite JS is identical in both harnesses. MOE_FROZEN_TEST_ONLY runs the selected arms, then exits. sh has set -e and no pipefail.
